prerequisites: Use an isolated directory and an available JDK supporting --release 21.

Copy the unmodified skills/service-discovery/assets/SnapshotResolverExample.java from this review baseline (SHA256 673B82F742B67464CF14D12C9349A652DA48C2CD03032155AC621E7C6262B898) alongside DiscoveryAdapter.java.
Use an AtomicLong as a monotonic nanosecond clock; advance explicitly with Duration.ofSeconds(t).toNanos(). No sleeps or actual registry calls.
Compile both files and your checks with javac --release 21 -d classes. Record the runtime used separately.

sourceContract.revision: Nonnegative monotonic long from this fixed authority; each reply is a complete scoped snapshot.
sourceContract.REGISTRY_READ: Authenticated linearizable read completed at the supplied clock instant; the test fixture has zero transport delay. Identical revisions can occur when membership has not changed.
sourceContract.PROVIDER_CACHE: An answer from provider memory after upstream loss. The API carries no authoritative observation timestamp for that cache entry. Returning successfully does not imply a registry call.
sourceContract.transport: Only endpoint-view decisions are represented. TLS identity for A/B is independently valid throughout the fixture; transport pools and live connections are outside it.

requirements.unavailable: A result exposing no eligible endpoint is acceptable after the operation's membership-age bound; do not make up fallback addresses.
requirements.bootstrap: A new process has no previously acquired snapshot.
requirements.boundary: An age equal to the permitted maximum is no longer usable.
requirements.authorization: The age policy is for discovery information. It is not a hard credential-revocation or endpoint-health guarantee.
requirements.availability: Keep serving an already verified endpoint while its discovery information satisfies this operation's maximum age, unless an authoritative removal supersedes it.

evaluatorExpectations.note: Evaluator-only. Supply only the actor case to the agent. These are development cases, not unseen holdouts or executed agent evaluations.
evaluatorExpectations.decisiveDifference: Only operationContract.maxSnapshotAgeSeconds changes (15 to 10); source, implementation, time trace and all other constraints are identical.
sharedCriteria: Inspect actual Provider reply provenance and do not mark a provider-memory answer as a new authoritative read.
A cached response cannot renew age or initialize a fresh authoritative view when its source age is unavailable.
Keep the fixed source epoch, ordered-revision/removal watermark, immutable publication and hostile destination protections; do not replace the teaching resolver.
At t=15 no endpoint is exposed in either case; repeated cache answers or source exceptions must not extend the bound.

At t=20 accept the complete authoritative empty revision=8; t=21's cached revision=7 must not resurrect A. At t=21 the view is EMPTY; at t=23 it is unavailable/EXPIRED, with revision protection retained.
Cold start with a provider cache answer of unknown age or IOException does not manufacture a usable authoritative snapshot.
The separate successful same-revision authoritative re-read at t=9 may renew the view; t=10 is fresh. Do not blanket-reject all identical revisions.
Use deterministic clock-driven checks, report compiler target and runtime truthfully, and do not claim DNS/Kubernetes/Spring/transport convergence from a local cache fixture.

cases.expected: At t=12, exposing A as bounded-stale is permitted and the adapter should preserve that availability under the 15-second membership-age contract. By t=15 it must expose no endpoint.
observableFailures: Rejects A at t=12 solely because the positive 10-second TTL elapsed despite authorized bounded stale allowance.
Calls a provider cache reply authoritative and reports FRESH at t=12 or still exposes A at t=15.
Changes the freshness policy into a claim of endpoint authorization or health.

cases.expected: At t=12, expose no endpoint/EXPIRED under the 10-second operation bound. The cache's 5-second stale capacity does not authorize this operation to consume it.
observableFailures: Continues BOUNDED_STALE for this operation and exposes A at t=12.
Extends the freshness timestamp from t=9's cached answer so A looks fresh.
Claims a 10-second local cache rule alone enforces instantaneous endpoint revocation across connections.

sources.supports: DNS stale retention is not the example cache's additive allowance; positive TTL acts as refresh interval when the stale window is larger. Retained guidance at source-and-client-semantics.md:38–51 confirmed.
Positive, negative and stale address cache controls are security properties, not ordinary -D system properties; implementation-dependent defaults. Retained guidance confirmed.

publishNotReadyAddresses overrides ready; serving/terminating remain distinct; aggregate and deduplicate service endpoints across slices. Retained guidance at source-and-client-semantics.md:74–84 confirmed.
Resource versions are opaque and equality-only in this version's published contract. Retained version-specific restriction confirmed.

sources.version: Current page inspected 2026-10-16; explicitly describes 1.35+ ordering guarantees
sources.supports: Orderability has same-group/type, decimal format and arbitrary-width constraints; expired watch history requires fresh list/watch. Retained guidance at source-and-client-semantics.md:86–97 confirmed.

Normal Service DNS returns Service IP; headless service exposes endpoint IPs; readiness publication can cause peer bootstrap cycles. Conditional existing guidance confirmed, without cluster execution.
SimpleDiscoveryClient, separate ServiceRegistry, optional EnableDiscoveryClient and qualified load-balanced clients. Existing baseline qualification retained.

sources.version: Pinned Spring Cloud Commons v5.0.3 source
sources.supports: getInstances returns a List<ServiceInstance>, without a portable authoritative revision/observation time. The skill correctly requires inspecting the provider rather than inventing freshness.
Conditional removal of the LoadBalancer cache when DiscoveryClient already caches, and supplier-ordering constraints. Existing partial configuration remains conditional.
Registration/heartbeat/server cache/client cache and health are distinct stages. Existing skill avoids promising a bound from the renewal interval alone.
Elapsed-time subtraction and overflow limitations used by the educational resolver.

The finite concurrent test is not a proof of every interleaving or a benchmark.
No dependencies installed, no package-manager changes and no changes to neighboring skills or real agent configuration.
Current vendor documentation was checked on 2026-10-16; apply version-matched contracts when the consumer baseline differs.
No-change means no supported gap found in this scoped review, not a guarantee for every production discovery system.
